deities: Many other Hindu gods and goddesses, floor by floor

history.period: 9th century CE (trawell.in) / 12th century CE (earthtrip.in, travel-review sources) / 'more than 400 years' (Zee Zest) - DISPUTED, verify before use
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: 'Trayambakeshwar Temple (Tera Manzil)' is the famous 13-storey Shiva temple on Laxman Jhula Road, Swarg Ashram, Rishikesh, on the eastern bank of the Ganges beside Lakshman Jhula (approx. 100 m away) - also listed as Kailash Niketan Temple on travel guides. It is a towering orange pyramid-shaped structure whose 13 ascending floors each house dozens of small shrines to different Hindu gods and goddesses (Shiva, Vishnu, Durga, Kali, Radha Krishna, the 12 Jyotirlingas, and others) - unusually, the temple is not dedicated to a single deity, though Shiva as Trayambakeshwar ('the abode of the three-eyed one') is the apex patron. The outer corridors double as handicraft and souvenir stalls; the 13th floor gives panoramic views of the Ganga and the Shivalik hills. DATE CONFLICT FLAG: travel sources credit founding to Adi Shankaracharya but date it anywhere from the 9th to the 12th century or merely '400+ years' - no primary source was found. JYOTIRLINGA MYTH FLAG: some travel reviews call it 'one of the 12 Jyotirlingas' - this is travel-site folklore, not canonical; the recognised Jyotirlinga is Trimbakeshwar in Nashik, Maharashtra. No lift; interior stairs only; photography is restricted inside; closed after the evening Ganga aarti.

name: Trayambakeshwar Temple (Tera Manzil)
town_description: The temple stands on Laxman Jhula Road in the Swarg Ashram area on the Tehri Garhwal side of the Ganges, right beside the Lakshman Jhula suspension bridge (~100 m) and about 5 km by road from Ram Jhula. Swarg Ashram is Rishikesh's ashram quarter, home to Parmarth Niketan, Gita Bhawan and the Beatles Ashram.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 24-35 km; sources differ)
travel.railway: Rishikesh Railway Station (approx. 6-9 km; sources differ)
travel.road: On Laxman Jhula Road, Swarg Ashram, ~100 m from Lakshman Jhula; ~5 km by road from Ram Jhula, ~12 km from Rishikesh main bus stand. Autos and taxis ply from anywhere in Rishikesh; parking near Lakshman Jhula is limited.

visitor_information.best_time: September-October and February-June; avoid July-August monsoon (damaged roads, few tourists) and December-January extreme cold
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM daily (consensus across travel guides); closed after the evening Ganga aarti (~8 PM). Free entry (footwear deposit ~Rs 10). Visit early morning (6-9 AM) for the calmest darshan; sunset from the upper floors is popular.
